solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Protect spades I kept outside

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

indicators.note: kept is placed outside the letter I, so held goes around it

parts.note: kept means held

explanation.surface: A card player guarding the spades in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts HELD around I, after S for spades.
explanation.definitionFit: To shield something is to guard or defend it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Edit most of Arsenic and Old Lace plot outline

indicators.note: to edit is to revise and rework, so the letters are rearranged
most of the play's title is kept, the opening run of it up to the O of Old

parts.note: the title of a famous comedy play and film

explanation.surface: Rewriting the plot of the comedy Arsenic and Old Lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' keeps ARSENIC and the O of Old; 'Edit' rearranges ARSENICO.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a written outline of a story or film's action, a sketch of the plot.

clue.text: Thankless types where the Ashes end up?

definitions.meaning: ashes from a fire collect in fire grates

explanation.surface: Ungrateful people and the destination of the Ashes cricket trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A in Ashes invokes the England-Australia cricket series; the real ashes are from a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrates are people who show no gratitude, so they are thankless by nature.

clue.text: Spoils officer guarding leaders in Oval Office

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so the officer goes around

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an army officer

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: Plunder, with an officer standing guard over the President's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' signals the enclosure; 'Spoils' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is plunder or booty, the same sense as spoils of war.

clue.text: This odd chap nicks paper from Corinth maybe

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of this are reworked
nicks means steals, so the chap takes the paper into himself

parts.note: a chap is a man
the i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: An eccentric man pinches a newspaper, apparently in ancient Corinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal and 'nicks' the insertion; the paper is the i, a British national daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmian describes the Isthmus of Corinth, home of the ancient Isthmian Games, so a Corinthian thing is one example.

clue.text: Adders collected, curbing hotel vacation course

parts.note: adders are people who add up, i.e. summers

indicators.note: curbing means restraining, so the first word holds the other in check inside it

parts.note: collected means calm, cool
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Snakes gathered together, held back by a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adders' are not snakes but people who add up; 'curbing' signals the insertion of the hotel letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A summer school is a course of study held during the long holidays.

clue.text: Terrifying Egyptian god split Osiris's first spears

indicators.note: spears means pierces, so the other letters go into the god's name

parts.note: Horus is the falcon-headed Egyptian god
to split is to rend

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Osiris's is used

explanation.surface: A frightening scene of an Egyptian god whose weapons pierce Osiris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spears' means pierces: the split-plus-initial run goes into the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrendous means dreadful or horrifying, close in sense to terrifying.

clue.text: Conceive international meeting without English

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the meeting surrounds the English letter

parts.note: a date is a meeting

explanation.surface: Imagining a world summit held without the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, putting DATE around E: D-E-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ideate is to form an idea or concept, so it means to think up or conceive.

clue.text: Wildlife function up river

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: tan is the tangent, a trigonometric function
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An animal habitat functioning upstream along a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAN into NAT, followed by URE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature is the living world of plants and animals, broadly the wildlife around us.

clue.text: Drink, say, going to be withdrawn? I quit

parts.note: say, meaning for example, gives EG

indicators.note: I quit tells us the letter I leaves the reversed word
withdrawn means pulled back, so the word going is read backwards

parts.note: the letter I as written

explanation.surface: Someone offered a drink, worried about being withdrawn, decides to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be withdrawn' reverses GOING to GNIOG, and 'I quit' then drops its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a festive beverage of eggs, milk and often spirits, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Soldiers rejected bloke coming out

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the soldiers are read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a bloke is a man, a gent

explanation.surface: Troops turning away a man who is leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns REME into EMER, followed by GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emergent is in the process of appearing or arising, which is what coming out describes.

clue.text: Smell Rod's silk that's fawn

parts.note: BO is body odour, a smell
a rod is a wand, and the 's adds S
crape is a crinkled silk fabric, also spelt crepe

explanation.surface: A smell given off by Rod's silk, which is light brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' poses as a colour of silk but is the verb to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To bow and scrape is to behave obsequiously, which is to fawn on someone.

clue.text: Somewhere to cook rare marine extract

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

explanation.surface: A kitchen stove used to prepare an unusual seafood extract.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly obtained from seaweed, so it is literally something extracted from the sea.

clue.text: Duck estate agent's billet-doux

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, and love is zero in tennis
an estate agent lets property, so is a letter

explanation.surface: A property agent dodging, or a duck owned by an agent: a bizarre romantic note.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'letter' here is one who lets houses, a sense only crosswords use.
explanation.definitionFit: Billet-doux is French for a sweet note, the romantic message sent between sweethearts.

clue.text: Dashing hero awards points for The Archers?

indicators.note: dashing means rushing about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gallant hero giving prizes on the radio soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' rearranges HERO and AWARDS. The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowheads are the pointed tips of arrows, the points archers shoot with.

clue.text: Cold drink violates America's code

indicators.note: to violate is to break or abuse, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something chilly breaks the laws of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violates' rearranges AMERICAS and CODE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice-cream soda is a chilled fizzy beverage with ice cream floating in it.

clue.text: Training detective force watching fences

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the watching word surrounds the others

parts.note: eyeing, also spelt eying, means watching
DI is a Detective Inspector
F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Police training: a detective force watching fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' is the enclosure signal; eying is an accepted spelling of eyeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Edifying means instructive or improving the mind, so it describes something that educates, a sense of training.

clue.text: Sign of maturity that needs clarification

definitions.meaning: read as a ... of hair, a mark of age

explanation.surface: Greying hair as a mark of age, and a matter left unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation where rules are vague; literally a greying patch shows age.

clue.text: Slight person chillier? Ought to be hugged

indicators.note: the second word is to be held inside the first, as if in an embrace

parts.note: chillier means colder
ought to is another way of saying should; 'to' belongs with the indicator

explanation.surface: A frosty person needs a warm embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be hugged' signals the enclosure; the definition is the verb phrase, to slight a person.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-shoulder someone is to ignore or rebuff them deliberately, which is to slight them.

clue.text: United Georgia and boring African country

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the word and goes inside

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A dull merger of United and Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' means drilling into, not dull: it signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is a landlocked nation in East Africa.

clue.text: Powerful trumpeter sacrificing limb

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up, so the limb is removed from the name

parts.note: Louis Armstrong was a famous jazz trumpeter
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A mighty musician giving up an arm for his art.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong and powerful are synonyms describing great force or might.

clue.text: Order given to butcher to be dismissed?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a request to a butcher to fetch a cut of meat
the idiom means to be sacked from a job

explanation.surface: A customer at a butcher's counter, and a worker being let go.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the chop is a slang way of losing one's job; literally it fetches a chop of meat.

clue.text: Dodgy moment after judge leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the judge's letter goes from the word

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: Something feels shady once the magistrate walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or suspect, the same sense as dodgy.

clue.text: Left top of grass or all of it

parts.note: an awn is the bristle at the tip of a grass flower

explanation.surface: Leaving the tips of the grass, or the whole lot, uncut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition refers back to grass: a lawn is a whole expanse of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is an area of mown turf, the whole stretch of grass rather than a single blade.

clue.text: Anne worked with a lot of recent arrivals

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A woman named Anne put in a lot of effort with newcomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges ANNE, A and LOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Neonatal relates to newborn babies, the newest arrivals into the world.

clue.text: Wheels round a sixth salted roe

indicators.note: the car goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Cars circling something, with a sixth portion of fish eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the enclosure; the inserted letters go after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is the salt-cured eggs of sturgeon, a luxury form of fish roe.

clue.text: Ships once leave small group of stars outside

indicators.note: the constellation is placed outside the other letters

parts.note: Aries is a constellation, the Ram
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Vessels of old departing, with a little constellation around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' signals the enclosure: the constellation wraps the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Argosies were large merchant sailing vessels of the past, so 'once' marks them as historical.

clue.text: Imagine stupidly ignoring current puzzle!

indicators.note: stupidly signals a rearrangement, and ignoring says some letters are left out of it

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Imagine foolishly paying no attention to the flow of things: a mystery!
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly ignoring' drops I (current) from IMAGINE and rearranges the rest, MAGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, the same sense as a puzzle.
